currentContext.strengths: Nearly eight decades of history as one of India's foremost storage battery manufacturers, with leadership across automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries|Five overseas technical collaborations and global technology alliances supporting an in-house R&D function|Expansive geographic footprint — exports to 72 countries|Nationwide distribution reach: 1,20,000+ channel partners, 60+ warehouses, 18,000+ rural touchpoints|Integrated recycling ecosystem via wholly-owned subsidiary Chloride Metals Limited, with ~79% of lead & lead-alloy requirements met through recycled inputs, strengthening resource efficiency and supply security|Influencer-led replacement-market conversion through the Samrat programme (18,000+ mechanics onboarded)|Zero-debt balance sheet with AAA (Stable)/A1+ ICRA ratings, giving financial flexibility to self-fund strategic investments through internal accruals
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen the lead-acid franchise, deepen product offerings, and build scalable capabilities in lithium-ion and advanced energy storage solutions|Treat investment in Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL) as a measured, long-term capital allocation decision to build domestic lithium-ion cell manufacturing capability, with emphasis on product quality, customer validation, localisation, operating discipline and return on capital|Maintain balance between preserving the cash-generating strength of the core lead-acid business and selectively investing for future growth|OEM strategy built around early-stage engagement with vehicle manufacturers — new product development, engineering, validation and product launch stages — to progressively expand across advanced lead-acid (ISS/EFB/AGM) and lithium-ion platforms|Deepen distribution and channel architecture through distributors, dealers, retailers, sub-dealers, the Samrat mechanic-influencer programme, paperless warranty registration and Exide Care touchpoints|Scale the solar business through in-house manufacturing of solar inverters, high-performance grid-tie inverters, the Exide Sunday digital platform, financing partnerships and empanelment under national solar programmes|Strengthen go-to-market and service capabilities through digital initiatives (SFDC/DMS integration) to improve data visibility, turnaround times and field productivity|Dividend distribution is governed by a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted 25th January 2017) under SEBI Listing Regulations. Payout decisions are calibrated to align shareholder returns with the Company's capital allocation priorities, balancing investment in capacity and technology for the core lead-acid business against the fund requirements of the upcoming EESL lithium-ion cell manufacturing project; the Board has decided to retain the entire remaining profit as retained earnings rather than transfer any amount to reserves.
currentContext.expansion: At Hosur, the Company enhanced capacity by 480K Medium VRLA batteries per annum through installation of globally sourced precision equipment (an Expander Line from TBS, UK; a Cast on Strap machine from BM, Austria; an Oxide Mill from Sovema, Italy; and an assembly line from TBS, UK); Plante plate processing capacity was expanded by 10K, with in-house mould manufacturing undertaken to retain technical expertise, alongside a new TM/LM (Low Maintenance) range and expanded SLI-AGM/AGMi portfolio. Continuous Casting Technology (CONCAST) was commissioned for industrial negative plates. Punch Grid Phase II for motorcycle batteries was completed, expanding Punch Grid battery capacity for 2-wheelers to 3.1 million units per month, with 90% of motorcycle batteries transitioned to Punch Grid Technology; automation and a comprehensive process-standardisation programme were also rolled out across motorcycle, SLI and industrial battery categories. Renewable capacity was expanded with 14 MWp of solar (Haryana) added during the year, taking total solar capacity to 95.3 MWp, complemented by 11.7 MW of wind capacity; water recovery at the Haldia factory reached ~80%. Separately, through wholly-owned subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL), the Company is building a greenfield lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility at the Hi-Tech Defence & Aerospace Park (Phase-II), Bengaluru, on an 80-acre site with planned capacity of 12 GWh in two phases of 6 GWh each; installation, integration and commissioning progressed across electrode manufacturing, cell assembly and formation processes during the year, with the cylindrical line (for 2-wheelers) under internal validation and customer sample supplies expected within a few months, and the prismatic line close to sample production with commissioning targeted for FY 2026-27. EESL's Prantij (Gujarat) facility currently manufactures battery modules and packs for EVs, telecom and energy storage applications.

risks.note: Potential disruptions from geopolitical uncertainties, regulatory realignments, cross-border trade restrictions, tariff changes and market volatility; flagged as a HIGH severity risk affecting the Company's manufacturing footprint, supply chain and cost competitiveness.

Challenges in aligning operations with environmental standards (emissions, water use, waste handling) alongside evolving ESG regulatory requirements; flagged as a HIGH severity risk tied to Economic Performance and Risk Management & Compliance.

External economic variables and sectoral factors may hinder cash generation and impact capital availability, a MODERATE severity risk mitigated through a debt-free capital structure, strong credit ratings and disciplined treasury practices.

Fluctuating raw material costs (principally lead, benchmarked to LME rates) affect cost structure, availability and margins, and expose the Company to longer delivery cycles; a MODERATE severity risk mitigated via sourcing diversification, inventory management, pricing/indexation clauses and increased use of recycled lead.

Cyber intrusions, data breaches and malicious attacks pose risk to operations, data integrity and brand trust; a MODERATE severity risk mitigated through a 24/7 Security Operations Center, VAPT assessments and simulation drills.

Inability to adapt to evolving battery technology (e.g., the lead-acid to lithium-ion transition) can impact competitiveness, product relevance, market share and customer expectations; a MODERATE severity risk being addressed through technology collaborations and expansion into electric mobility.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

hero.oneLiner: Exide is one of India's leading storage battery manufacturers, with a diversified lead-acid battery portfolio across automotive and industrial applications and an emerging lithium-ion cell manufacturing capability through its subsidiary EESL.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Exide is one of India's leading storage battery manufacturers, with a diversified lead-acid battery portfolio across automotive and industrial applications and an emerging lithium-ion cell manufacturing capability through its subsidiary EESL.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Exide manufactures and sells lead-acid batteries and accumulators (conventional flooded as well as Valve-Regulated Lead-Acid/VRLA batteries) for automotive OEMs, automotive aftermarket/replacement, home inverters, industrial UPS, telecom, solar, industrial infrastructure (railways, traction, data centres, power & projects, defence) and submarine applications. It also exports automotive, traction and reserve power batteries, and is building a lithium-ion cell, module and battery-pack business through wholly-owned subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL), backed by an integrated lead-recycling ecosystem through wholly-owned subsidiary Chloride Metals Limited (CML).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

- **Automotive Aftermarket Batteries:** motorcycle batteries, passenger vehicle batteries, commercial vehicle batteries
- **Home Batteries & Inverters:** EL-ULTRA, INVAMAGIC, High Backup series, POWERBOX
- **Industrial UPS:** EP range, EL range
- **Industrial Infrastructure:** railway batteries, traction batteries, data centre batteries, power & projects batteries, defence batteries

- **Last Mile Connectivity:** e-rickshaw and last-mile mobility batteries
- **Telecom:** telecom backup power batteries
- **New Energy Business (EESL):** lithium-ion cells, modules, battery packs
- **Lead Recycling Business (CML):** recycled lead and lead alloys, recycled plastic

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Replacement demand expected to stay healthy, supported by improving replacement cycles, ageing of the Medium & Heavy Commercial Vehicle fleet, and rising preference for organised/trusted brands
- OEM demand strengthening with higher vehicle production, new model launches, improving rural demand and better financing availability
- Industrial UPS growth supported by outperformance in higher ampere-hour categories, continued VRLA preference and institutional business expansion via the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), though overall market growth remains measured due to cautious private capex and project-linked procurement cycles
- Railways, traction and data centres seen as long-term structural opportunities — metro projects (Bangalore, Mumbai, Agra, Kanpur) progressing toward commissioning — while power & projects demand remained uneven as thermal power tenders were deferred
- Solar rooftop adoption and policy support (PLI scheme, PM Surya Ghar) driving strong double-digit growth; the solar business surpassed Rs 1,000 crore in annual revenue for the first time
- Telecom segment facing structural headwinds from the transition toward lithium-ion technology, requiring portfolio recalibration
- International/export business remained under pressure from geopolitical dynamics and tariff challenges, with exports declining significantly year-on-year
- Lead-acid batteries expected to remain relevant on safety, cost-competitiveness and proven performance even as lithium-ion gains share in select applications, viewed as an additional technology stream rather than a full substitute
- GST 2.0 rationalisation and easing inflation supported a demand recovery in the second half of FY 2025-26 after a relatively subdued first half
- FY 2026-27 outlook: geopolitical tensions (particularly West Asia) and inflationary/interest-rate pressures could temper demand, but opportunities remain robust across automotive replacement and OEMs, solar, railways, industrial UPS, traction and infrastructure-linked segments
- Industrial Infrastructure business outlook described as improving and compelling, supported by a healthy enquiry pipeline, even as growth across certain core sectors remains measured
- EESL continues to engage with 2-wheeler, 3-wheeler, 4-wheeler and stationary energy OEMs across key end markets, with initial commercial dispatches expected to commence in FY 2026-27

Punch Grid Phase II for motorcycle batteries was completed, expanding Punch Grid battery capacity for 2-wheelers to 3.1 million units per month, with 90% of motorcycle batteries transitioned to Punch Grid Technology; automation and a comprehensive process-standardisation programme were also rolled out across motorcycle, SLI and industrial battery categories. Renewable capacity was expanded with 14 MWp of solar (Haryana) added during the year, taking total solar capacity to 95.3 MWp, complemented by 11.7 MW of wind capacity; water recovery at the Haldia factory reached ~80%. Separately, through wholly-owned subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL), the Company is building a greenfield lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility at the Hi-Tech Defence & Aerospace Park (Phase-II), Bengaluru, on an 80-acre site with planned capacity of 12 GWh in two phases of 6 GWh each; installation, integration and commissioning progressed across electrode manufacturing, cell assembly and formation processes during the year, with the cylindrical line (for 2-wheelers) under internal validation and customer sample supplies expected within a few months, and the prismatic line close to sample production with commissioning targeted for FY 2026-27. EESL's Prantij (Gujarat) facility currently manufactures battery modules and packs for EVs, telecom and energy storage applications.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Nearly eight decades of history as one of India's foremost storage battery manufacturers, with leadership across automotive and industrial lead-acid batteries
- Five overseas technical collaborations and global technology alliances supporting an in-house R&D function
- Expansive geographic footprint — exports to 72 countries
- Nationwide distribution reach: 1,20,000+ channel partners, 60+ warehouses, 18,000+ rural touchpoints
- Integrated recycling ecosystem via wholly-owned subsidiary Chloride Metals Limited, with ~79% of lead & lead-alloy requirements met through recycled inputs, strengthening resource efficiency and supply security
- Influencer-led replacement-market conversion through the Samrat programme (18,000+ mechanics onboarded)
- Zero-debt balance sheet with AAA (Stable)/A1+ ICRA ratings, giving financial flexibility to self-fund strategic investments through internal accruals

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Commodity volatility (sulfur, plastic, LPG, lead, lithium); rupee depreciation; geopolitical disruption to exports; lithium-ion yield ramp-up delays; OEM contract lag in price pass-through; government policy delay for PLI/incentives

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Sulfuric acid cost surge is tied to petrochemical refinery utilization (sulfur byproduct), not just demand; Exide’s Li-ion pricing strategy hinges on China’s VAT hike (9% increase by Jan 2027) and localization incentives; Telecom decline is structural, not cyclical — Li-ion replacement is permanent; 92% of business grew double-digit despite 8% decline in exports/Telecom

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the lead-acid franchise, deepen product offerings, and build scalable capabilities in lithium-ion and advanced energy storage solutions
- Treat investment in Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL) as a measured, long-term capital allocation decision to build domestic lithium-ion cell manufacturing capability, with emphasis on product quality, customer validation, localisation, operating discipline and return on capital
- Maintain balance between preserving the cash-generating strength of the core lead-acid business and selectively investing for future growth
